key_insight: Instead of widening latent channels to preserve quality at high compression, TC-AE unlocks representational capacity by operating in the token space of a ViT-based autoencoder, preventing latent collapse and maintaining reconstruction/generative fidelity with simpler models.
problem_solved: Latent representation collapse and degraded generative/reconstruction performance that arise when existing deep-compression AEs try to maintain quality by merely increasing latent channel counts under high compression ratios.
method: Design a ViT-based encoder–decoder that treats the bottleneck as a token space rather than a high-channel tensor.
Increase and utilize token capacity (more informative tokens or richer token interactions) to encode compressed latents instead of scaling channel width.
Introduce token-space operations/constraints that preserve diversity and prevent collapse, enabling stable training without multi-stage schemes or extreme architectural scaling.
impact: Enables more compact, stable deep-compression autoencoders that keep reconstruction and generative quality at high compression ratios while avoiding costly channel scaling or complicated training pipelines — useful for efficient storage, transmission, and generative tasks.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: input → patch/tokenization → ViT-based encoder → token bottleneck → ViT-based decoder → output (reconstruction)
Before vs after illustration: latent collapse when increasing channels vs preserved diversity using token-capacity approach
Performance chart: reconstruction quality / FID vs compression ratio comparing channel-scaling baselines and TC-AE
Icon set: tokens (small squares) vs channels (wide bars) to convey the conceptual shift from channel width to token capacity
paper_title: TC-AE: Unlocking Token Capacity for Deep Compression Autoencoders
paper_authors: Teng Li, Ziyuan Huang, Cong Chen, Yangfu Li, Yuanhuiyi Lyu
